about: 16 section and page grounds drawn in CSS (backgrounds.css). One class on a section, a wrapper, body or a visual's panel. The twelve section grounds set the page tokens for their children; the two page grounds (paper, topglow) set none and only paint. Each works on light and dark palettes and keeps ink 7:1 and muted 4.5:1 on its text zone (check.mjs measures it). pick.mjs deals a page's grounds (at most 2 beyond the flat tokens, no page ground; paper and grain are marked dealt:false and never dealt, since a ground with grain is the page's one effect; --effect also skips the grounds marked texture), for software, tech and gaming pages only (VI-41, VI-42): a product, service or place page is flat and no ground is listed for it (a product page with a technical subject asks with --kind tech and is dealt as software). Grounds list the sections they fit (sections): pick.mjs deals those; strict ones go nowhere else, byRole ones (band, field) also fit by role when the plan has none of their ids. Grounds marked coloured (band, field, stage; grain is never dealt) count toward the one coloured ground every page of five sections or more holds.

weights.2: medium: a visible change of ground
weights.3: loud: the one section a screen remembers

kinds.soft: paints no colour of its own and fades into the page at the top and bottom; neighbours anything
kinds.hard: a band with its own colour and edges (add bg-inset for a rounded panel on the grid)
kinds.page: a ground for the whole page (body or one wrapper), not for one section
kinds.panel: a rounded panel behind one visual (bg-stage): vivid, with no text of its own; every word on it sits on a card

modifiers.bg-inset: a hard ground as a rounded panel whose left and right edges sit on the container's
modifiers.bg-photo--left: the photograph's scrim from the left, for words in the middle of the left side
modifiers.bg-photo--light: the scrim from the light side and dark words, for a pale photograph
modifiers.bg-tint: with bg-band or bg-field: the second tone is a pale tint of the accent's own colour (a mint for a teal accent) instead of the lit ground, so the band is coloured on a sand page
modifiers.bg-bleed: on a dark page a band or a field is inset automatically (a pale slab is the brightest thing there); bg-bleed keeps it full-bleed

knobs.--g-hue: the colour the tints lean to; default the accent with a hue guard (never violet or lavender)
knobs.--g-k: strength of the tints, 1 by default
knobs.--tone / --tone-ink: the second brand tone and its text colour for bg-band and bg-field; default the lit ground
knobs.--g-photo: url(...) for bg-photo when no child is used
knobs.--g-screen: a ground section's minimum height (default min(88svh, 860px) for a hard ground, min(76svh, 760px) for a soft one); 0px = the words' own height
knobs.--g-photo-pos: where the subject of the photograph sits (object-position); --g-photo-pos-m on a phone
knobs.--scrim-h: how high the photograph's scrim stays deep: backgrounds.js measures the words and sets it; a value the section sets is kept

grounds.name: Mist
grounds.mood: airy, soft colour fields like a wash of light in two neighbouring hues
grounds.where: a section head over a row of three open cards; a feature list; any section that needs a little colour

grounds.name: Halo
grounds.mood: calm, one light behind one thought
grounds.where: a centred statement or a closing line: a heading, a few lines and a button. Move it with --halo-x and --halo-y to where the heading sits

grounds.name: Grain
grounds.mood: tactile, a tinted field with a fine film grain, a light corner and two neighbouring hues
grounds.where: a split with text on the left and one UI card on the right (the Figma tile); a feature on a field

grounds.name: Paper
grounds.mood: quiet, a page ground that is never flat
grounds.where: on body or one wrapper: fine grain and a faint tint at the top and bottom. Soft grounds are transparent, so it shows through them; hard grounds cover it

grounds.name: Dusk
grounds.mood: gentle, one tone becomes the next with no edge: both ends melt into whatever the page paints there
grounds.where: a quote with one big number, a proof section, any section between two plain ones. Set --g-to for the tone, --g-from and --g-next to melt from or into a colour instead of the page

grounds.name: Top glow
grounds.mood: clean, light under the nav that the page lifts out of
grounds.where: a wrapper around the nav and the hero: a glow from the top edge and a thin lit line. The hero's ground for software and service pages

grounds.name: Ruled
grounds.mood: precise, a grid that is the page's own frame: its first and last rules lie on the container's edges, it fades toward the top and bottom and is clear behind the heading
grounds.where: a centred hero or statement, a section with one big visual. Never over a table, pricing, a list or any section that draws row rules of its own

grounds.name: Dots
grounds.mood: quiet texture: a dot field in the margins and corners, clear behind the heading and the words
grounds.where: a centred section with a row of figures, a logo row, an integrations section: a dot field and a pool of light behind the heading

grounds.name: Arcs
grounds.mood: open, rings that rise from below like x.ai's footer
grounds.where: the closing call to action, or the section above the footer: a heading and a button over rings

grounds.name: Band
grounds.mood: warm, a coloured band in the page's second tone, lit from one corner and deeper in the other
grounds.where: one big number and a UI card; one statement with a button. The tone is the lit ground (sand, sky, sage, painting) or --tone. On a dark page it is the one light band

grounds.name: Field
grounds.mood: rich, a grainy gradient in one family of colour (a peach beside sand, a cyan beside sky) with a light sweep: Figma's sand tile
grounds.where: a centred heading over one or two UI cards; best as a rounded inset panel (bg-inset)

grounds.name: Stage
grounds.mood: vivid, the accent as a grainy mesh that one card floats on: Figma's colour tiles
grounds.where: the panel behind the one UI card or window beside a section's text (it is a panel, not a section: <div class="bg-stage"><div class="mini">). Never behind a heading: every word on it is on a card. On a strong-colour page (data-tint away) it takes the accent's hue, on a grey accent (data-lowchroma) the lit ground's colour. --stage-w is the card's width

grounds.name: Photo
grounds.mood: calm and large, a photograph under a quiet scrim
grounds.where: a media band, the hero of a place or product page, a closing photo. Put the photograph in as (or --g-photo: url(...) where no img fits); words sit lower left (bg-photo--left: left side). A pale photograph takes bg-photo--light (dark words on a light scrim). Credits go in the footer line
grounds.needs: a vetted photograph with a calm area (scripts/photos.mjs pick)

variants.note: a white photograph under the dark scrim: the worst case for white words

grounds.name: Horizon
grounds.mood: dramatic, a dark band with a lit curve like a planet's rim
grounds.where: a statement the page is sure of (security, scale, a promise) with a button above the horizon; the page's one dark band. Words stay above the lit curve, whose rim is brightest at the top

grounds.name: Deep
grounds.mood: quiet and dark, near-black with a cool pool at the top, a lit lip and grain like x.ai
grounds.where: a feature section with two or three UI cards (chat, code, voice): the dark ground UI reads best on

grounds.name: Liquid
grounds.mood: alive, two slow blobs of two neighbouring hues drifting; transforms only
grounds.where: a call to action or a hero with a heading and two buttons. One a page; it is the page's moving thing, so no other looping effect in view
